correctness.rationale: For a shared uniform phase, the fractional-part carry is 0 or 1, and subtracting 1/2 gives the sum of two centered sawtooths minus the common slope-d sawtooth. The Fourier coefficient at nonzero n equals -W_j(n)/(2π i n); taking the conjugate in Parseval gives the positive factor 1/(2π²) on the sum over n>0. When d does not divide n all W are nonnegative; when d divides n the two positive terms total at most d, so all are nonpositive. At n=d both positive terms occur iff j and d-j divide d, equivalent to d/j=d/(d-j)=2. Therefore any pair with both indices noncentral has a strictly positive contribution from n=d, and no opposite-sign term. Summing over common multiples of a,b recovers gcd(a,b)^2/(12ab); expanding produces the eight gcd terms plus the unit term. Marginals 1/2 then determine all four cells. The diagonal and equal complementary coordinates are valid special cases, and discontinuities have probability zero. Independent exact right-continuous integration on 968 pair instances across 3≤d≤18 agreed, including 22 zero cases all involving the center; replay `python3 /workspace/audit_checks/frozen_reconstruction.py`. The finite test does not prove the sign theorem. Nothing here transfers to sums of actual prime-adic valuations.
